matchstick.title: Balance by numeric difference and single‑stick transformation
matchstick.principle: Compute the integer values of both sides of the equation, find the numeric difference, and then look for a single‑matchstick move that changes a numeral’s value by exactly that amount while keeping all symbols valid Roman numerals.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the displayed equation is false and the numeric values of the left‑hand side and right‑hand side can be evaluated.
matchstick.example: Moving a stick that changes a V into an L (adding 45) when the equation is only off by 5, leaving the equality still false.

matchstick.title: Convert V to X to add 5
matchstick.principle: If the imbalance is exactly 5, turn a V (value 5) into an X (value 10) by repositioning one of its diagonal sticks so the two sticks cross; this raises that numeral’s value by 5.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation is off by 5 and a V appears that can be reshaped into an X without breaking other symbols.
matchstick.example: Changing a V into an L (value 50) when only a +5 adjustment is needed, which makes the equation incorrect.

matchstick.title: Swap I and V in IV to make VI (adds 2)
matchstick.principle: If the imbalance is exactly 2 and the pattern IV appears, move the I stick to the right of the V, turning IV (4) into VI (6) and increasing the numeral’s value by 2.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation is off by 2 and a numeral IV is present on either side.
matchstick.example: Removing the I stick from IV and leaving a single diagonal stick, which is not a valid numeral, instead of correctly forming VI.
